passages.quote:
To find out which notes apply to you, check the description in the top right-hand corner of your CT620 notice. You’ll find one of the following references:

CT620 AMD

CT620 AMK

CT620 ASA

CT620 CLA

CT620 CLO

CT620 COR

CT620 DET

CT620 DIS

Use this reference to find the information in these notes that applies to you.

If you believe that your CT620 notice is asking you to pay too little tax, you must tell HMRC within 30 days of the date on the notice.

If you fail to tell us that you’ve underpaid tax, or do not pay an amount due by the date requested, HMRC may charge you interest or apply a penalty.

Your CT620 notice provides detailed information about your tax position. You can contact the Corporation Tax Helpline if you need more support.

If you’ve already authorised an adviser to act on your behalf, we’ll have sent them a copy of your CT620 notice. If you need to authorise an adviser or agent to act on your behalf, you’ll need to complete a 64-8 paper form or apply online.

CT620 AMD — amendment to a Company Tax Return

This CT620 notice explains our revised calculations, including:

any tax you need to pay

information about overpayments of tax you may have made

If you fail to tell us that you’ve underpaid tax, or do not pay an amount due by the date requested, HMRC may charge you interest or apply a penalty.

Read section ‘Payment of tax’ for information about paying your tax or overpayments.

You can appeal against this amendment within 30 days of us notifying you of the amendment — read section ‘Appeals’ for more information.

CT620 AMK — acknowledgement

This CT620 notice confirms that we have received your amendment. It includes information about:

any tax you need to pay based on your calculations

any overpayments of tax you may have made

If you fail to tell us that you’ve underpaid tax, or do not pay an amount due by the date requested, HMRC may charge you interest or apply a penalty.

If you’re due a repayment, we will contact you separately. Read section ‘Payment of tax’ for information about paying your tax or overpayments.

This acknowledgement does not mean that we agree with your calculations, as we may still correct the Company Tax Return or open an enquiry.

When we can correct a return or open an enquiry

We can only correct a return, amended return or claim within 9 months of the date we received it.

The time limit for opening an enquiry depends on when we received the return. We can open an enquiry:

within 12 months of receiving most returns submitted on or before the filing date

within 12 months of the filing date if the return was submitted on or before the filing date by a company that is a member of a group — this does not include small groups

for returns submitted after the filing date, up to and including the next specified date after 12 months from the date we received the return — these dates are:

31 January

30 April

31 July

31 October

We can open an enquiry into an amended return, claim (or election), or amended claim made outside of a return. We can do this up to and including the next specified date after 12 months from the date the amendment or claim was made. These dates are:

31 January

30 April

31 July

31 October

When you can amend a return

You can amend your return within 12 months of the filing date. This is usually within 2 years of the end of the accounting period.

You can amend a claim made outside of a return within 12 months of the date the claim was made.

CT620 ASA — amendment of Self Assessment

This CT620 notice explains our revised calculation of your company’s Self Assessment and any tax you need to pay.

If you fail to tell us that you’ve underpaid tax, or do not pay an amount due by the date requested, HMRC may charge you interest or apply a penalty.

If you’re due a repayment, we will contact you separately. Read section ‘Payment of tax’ for information about paying your tax or overpayments.

You can appeal against this amendment within 30 days of us notifying you of the amendment — read section ‘Appeals’ for more information.

CT620 CLA — claims

This CT620 notice explains how your tax position may have changed because you did not include a claim (or election) in your Company Tax Return. It shows our revised calculations, including:

any tax you need to pay

information about overpayments of tax you may have made

If you fail to tell us that you’ve underpaid tax, or do not pay an amount due by the date requested, HMRC may charge you interest or apply a penalty.

If you’re due a repayment, we will contact you separately. Read section ‘Payment of tax’ for information about paying your tax or overpayments.

When we can correct a claim

We can correct missing or incorrect information in a claim. This can include errors in how the claim was made or calculated.

If we make a correction, we will include a note explaining this. We can only make a correction within 9 months of the date you made the claim.

When you can amend a claim or challenge a correction

You can amend a claim within 12 months of the date you made it. This includes claims made outside your Company Tax Return.

You cannot appeal against this correction.

CT620 CLO — completion of an enquiry

This CT620 notice confirms that we have completed our enquiry into your Company Tax Return. It includes information about:

our findings and any changes to your return

any tax you need to pay

If you fail to tell us that you’ve underpaid tax, or do not pay an amount due by the date requested, HMRC may charge you interest or apply a penalty.

Read section ‘Payment of tax’ for information about paying your tax or overpayments.

The enquiry may include estimated figures — read section ‘Estimated figures’ for more information.

You can appeal against this amendment within 30 days of us notifying you of the amendment — read section ‘Appeals’ for more information.

Your request to postpone payment must include:

the reason you think the amount charged is too high and by how much

how much you propose to pay while your appeal is being considered

If a postponed amount is later found to be payable, we will charge you interest from the original due date. We will tell you whether we agree to postpone your payment.

You must pay any tax that has not been postponed immediately.

After we receive your appeal

We may contact you to discuss the dispute and try to resolve it.

We will always write to you regarding the outcome of your appeal. You can ask us to review a decision, or we may offer you a review.

Appeal to a tribunal

You can ask for an independent tribunal to hear your appeal.

If you accept our offer of a review, or ask us to review the case, you can only appeal to a tribunal after the review has ended.

If you disagree with the review decision, you can ask for an independent tribunal to hear your appeal. You must do this within 30 days of the date shown on the:

conclusion of review letter

letter telling you that the review is treated as upholding the original decision

To appeal to the tribunal, write to the HM Courts and Tribunals Service or complete a tribunal appeal form.

You can only ask the tribunal to consider your appeal if you have already appealed to HMRC.

Estimated figures

We may estimate your company’s income, losses or tax if we do not hold enough information. Estimated figures are identified by displaying an ‘E’ before a figure.

We may make an estimate when:

your company did not submit a return

following an enquiry, we believe a return is incorrect and we have not agreed the figures with you

after an enquiry, or when it is too late to start one, we discover you have been under-assessed because:

not all relevant facts were disclosed

we believe you, or someone acting on your behalf, acted negligently or fraudulently

More information

Read about Corporation Tax payment deadlines.

You can contact the Corporation Tax Helpline if you need more support.
